smm_pool.title: Ads Super Burst, First Impression Ads, and Aggregated View Time
smm_pool.text: During the recent Brand Building Summit , Meta shared several updates. Here are the details of three new ad features… 1. Ads Super Burst Ads Super Burst allows advertisers to book a window of three to 24 hours to reach your audience. With category exclusivity, no other advertiser in your category can book the same window. Meta suggests this might be used around a product launch, promoting an external event, or the first weekend of a new sports season. You can plan these campaigns in Reach Planner to secure inventory during your desired dates. 2. First Impression Ads Meta says that advertisers have asked for the first ad position in feeds for years, and now it’s being offered as a test in the US. Reserve the first ad spot that users see when they open their feeds. Nothing about the ad unit will look any different from your typical feed ads, but only one brand will have access to this prime location per day during the test. My concern is what this could do to performance of other ad placements. If Meta is saying that the first ad in feed performs best and that spot can be reserved, wouldn’t it suggest that other advertisers will have less access to this ad spot when they don’t reserve it? And if that’s the case, won’t overall performance suffer? 3. Aggregated View Time This is a new way to measure video ad performance. Instead of just looking at a single video view (continuous 2-second view or ThruPlay view), Meta takes an aggregated approach. This metric finds the average total view time people saw all of your videos during a single week. For now, Aggregated View Time is only a metric that you can use in reporting.
